Move is stated generally (goal shape ∃ n, c ≤ S n with a general lower bound B n ≤ S n; witness found by inverting the bound), and consequences are honest and grounded. But the 'when not to use' clause contains a factually wrong illustration: it says 'the bound only approaches 4 in the limit — an exact 3.999 at a finite n is then impossible', yet the entry's own point is that 4·3999/4000 = 3.999 exactly, i.e. 3.999 IS attained at finite n (n=4000). This directly contradicts the entry and would mislead a reader about when the move applies. Fix: reword the example to a target the bound genuinely never reaches, e.g. 'the bound 4n/(n+1) only approaches 4 from below, so a target of 4 itself is never attained at any finite n and the comparison will not close'.
